newsitem.title: CHINA: China to launch value-added tax probe.
newsitem.headline: China to launch value-added tax probe.

text.p: China will launch a probe of value-added tax payments due to serious problems with "abnormal" tax declarations, the Economic Information Daily said on Thursday.

The State Administration of Taxation would investigate more than 10 percent of all commercial firms in cities and towns, particularly those with unusual changes in sales and value-added tax last year, it said.
The focus of the probe would be on wholesale and retail vendors, the report said.
Problems with the value-added tax were considered to be serious, providing opportunities for economic crime through the use of value-added tax receipts, it said.
Tax payment in the commercial sector was declining, affecting state tax income, it said without giving details.
China collected 71.054 billion yuan ($8.56 billion) in value-added taxes in the first quarter, up 15.1 percent compared with the year-ago period.
